thread:
carol-support: customer reporting repeated 504s hitting /v1/generate. 6 x 504 in last 10m, sample req id req-0a1b2c. customer says latency spikes then gateway timeouts. escalating to oncall. logs attached (short snippet).

sre-oncall: on it. can you paste a minimal repro curl and the request headers they sent? also which cluster/tenant ID?

carol-support: tenant: acme-inc. curl they used: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}' -v```

maya-runtime: looking at serving dashboards — surge started ~4867889700. Gateway 504s coincide with scale-up events. KEDA ScaledObject didn't create new pods fast enough; readiness/warmup delay ~35s per pod. HPA wanted to scale but actual pod count stayed at 1 for a while.

jonah-eng: I see KEDA logs around that time showing failures fetching metrics: `error fetching external metric: 403 Forbidden` for metrics from billing/queue-proxy. If scaler can't read queue length, it won't trigger scale. any auth errors in proxy logs?

alice-platform: checked the proxy logs — token refresh to metrics backend failed with `401 token_expired` repeated during rotation window at 4867889662. metrics endpoint returned 401 -> KEDA treated metric as absent.

miguel-cs: customer says they saw initial successful requests then sudden 504s for ~3 minutes, then partial recovery. They raised cost concern about keeping min pods high. want root cause and repro for postmortem.

sre-oncall: can we reproduce locally? steps to recreate: 1) create a ScaledObject hooked to external metrics (queue-length) 2) simulate a short-lived auth error to metrics (return 401 for 60s) 3) flood traffic to endpoint to force scale.

maya-runtime: repro notes: reproduced in staging — when metrics backend returns 401 during token rotation, KEDA flags the metric as invalid and doesn't scale. Meanwhile HPA doesn't fill the gap because our HPA target is CPU-based and CPU stayed low until warmwarmcache/throttles. Net effect: queue backlog grows -> gateway 504s.

jonah-eng: mitigation applied to prod: bumped minReplicas from 1 -> 3 for affected service and increased KEDA poll frequency (short term). applied a guarded rollout. customer back to normal.

alice-platform: patch we applied: ```kubectl patch deployment inference-svc -p '{"spec":{"replicas":3}}' && kubectl annotate scaledobject inference-scaler keda.k8s.io/polling-interval=5``` (rolled via canary).

carol-support: customer confirmed reduction of 504s after patch. they still want a repeatable fix (not manual bump).

sre-oncall: follow-ups: 1) add alert when KEDA external metric returns 4xx/5xx for >30s 2) add fallback policy so HPA uses an additional queue-based metric if KEDA is unavailable 3) short-term playbook we can run rapidly (bump minReplicas, increase poll).

jonah-eng: root cause summary for postmortem: token rotation caused transient 401s from metrics backend -> KEDA treated metric as unavailable -> scaler did not increase pods -> HPA tied to CPU did not react fast enough -> warmup delay of new pods -> gateway timed out requests (504). also note a race between our metrics proxy rotation and KMS key refresh.

billing-bot: note: billing service API reported a 45s token-rotation window at 4867889658 (incident #INC-2026-342).

alice-platform: long-term fix ideas: - make KEDA resilient to transient metric auth errors (treat 401/403 for Xs as retryable) - add a controller-level fallback that triggers emergency scale when queue depth > threshold even if external metric fetch fails - improve token rotation handoff with zero-downtime refresh (staggered keys)

miguel-cs: customer wants timeline and RCA, I'll draft an email with mitigation steps we took and ETA for fixes.

carol-support: thanks team. saving logs and repro steps to the incident ticket. tagging for postmortem: @postmortem.

sre-oncall: assigning follow-ups: jira INF-1721 (alert + fallback), INF-1722 (KEDA retry logic), INF-1723 (token rotation hardening). closing slack thread when tickets ack'd.
